formNote: The Shuowen: 時，四時也 — “the four seasons.” Mojidata IDS: ⿰日寺. Time is first the sun’s round of seasons.
summary: The seasons, time, and the timely: for Mencius, Confucius was the sage of timeliness. In the Yijing, wisdom is acting in step with the moment, 與時偕行.
placement: Below the centre on the right, beside 易. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Four Seasons
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen: 時，四時也, “the four seasons”, with 日, the sun, as meaning and 寺 as sound. Time begins as the year’s turning.

satellites.title: The Sage of the Timely
satellites.evidence: Mencius 5B1 compares the sages: Bo Yi the pure, Yi Yin the responsible, Liuxia Hui the accommodating, and 孔子，聖之時者也 — “Confucius was the sage of timeliness”: he did what each moment asked.

satellites.title: Timely, Not Merely Timed
satellites.evidence: Greek separates χρόνος, time as duration, from καιρός, the fitting moment. When Mencius calls Confucius 聖之時者, the sage of timeliness, 時 leans toward kairos: not how long, but when it is right.
satellites.caveat: An analogy of senses, not a translation. 時 also plainly means the seasons and the hour, and kairos carries its own rhetorical and theological history.
